sources.note: Reformulates chart question answering as a chain in which every reasoning step carries a predicted image region, trains that pairing through a curriculum graded by nesting depth, and finds explicit intermediate grounding worth 8.78 points over letting the model attend implicitly.
sources.title: CURV: Enhancing Chart Understanding Through Curriculum Visual Grounded Reasoning

sources.note: Turns table-to-report generation into Monte Carlo tree search over partial reports, scored by a reward that verifies every numerical claim by generating and executing SQL against the source table rather than by asking a judge — and keeps that search reward strictly separate from the benchmark's own evaluator to avoid a reward-hacking loop.
sources.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search for Table-to-Multimodal Report Generation

sources.note: Benchmarks whether multimodal models can construct visual aids for geometry problems, and finds high answer accuracy conceals near-total failure at producing or reasoning from those aids.
sources.title: VisAidMath: Benchmarking Visual-Aided Mathematical Reasoning

sources.note: Identifies a multimodal failure where models see the risky visual cue but let narrative coherence override safety as reasoning proceeds, and defends against it by extracting intent before generation.
sources.title: Mitigating Safety Context Amnesia in Multimodal Reasoning Models via Intent-Guided Safety Reasoning

sources.note: A university-level multimodal math benchmark with original, hand-drawn, photographed and text-only variants of each problem, on which a model with no image beats its own multimodal variants and GPT-5.
sources.title: MathSight: A Benchmark Exploring Have Vision-Language Models Really Seen in University-Level Mathematical Reasoning?

sources.note: Benchmarks multimodal models on detecting and categorizing errors in K-12 math solutions collected from real student interactions, with the best model about 10% behind human experts.
sources.title: ErrorRadar: Benchmarking Complex Mathematical Reasoning of Multimodal Large Language Models Via Error Detection

sources.note: A multimodal scientific reasoning benchmark over 54 subfields with domain-specific visuals and expert solutions for 46% of items, scoring the reasoning process as well as the answer.
sources.title: SciVQR: A Multidisciplinary Multimodal Benchmark for Advanced Scientific Reasoning Evaluation

instructions:
Write the wiki definition for 'multimodal reasoning'.

The sources below are every archived paper and talk that mentions it. Define it as they use it: if they disagree, say so; if the term is used loosely, say that too.

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

result.definition: Reasoning that must combine visual and textual evidence, and across 7 sources a setting where the archive's recurring finding is that answer accuracy conceals whether the image was used at all. Three measurements make that concrete. A visual-aid benchmark finds high answer accuracy hiding near-total failure at producing or reasoning from the aids the problems require. A university-level mathematics benchmark with original, hand-drawn, photographed and text-only variants finds a model given no image beating its own multimodal variants and a frontier system. And test-time selection fails for a structural reason -- neither answer frequency nor verbalised confidence tests whether an answer depends on the pixels, so a grounded answer and a confident language-prior guess look identical at the selection layer. Two failure modes specific to the modality: a model can see a risky visual cue and let narrative coherence override it as reasoning proceeds, and explicit intermediate grounding is worth 8.78 points over letting the model attend implicitly. The corpus's general verdict is that leading proprietary and open models remain significantly limited on complex multimodal reasoning, and that the reasoning process itself introduces vulnerabilities the single-modality case does not have.
